newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds rose sharply on Friday afternoon in response to lower than expected August U.S. CPI data, but the market failed to draw investors' interest, dealers said.
U.S. August consumer prices rose a modest 0.1 percent in August, below forecasts of +0.2 percent. Treasuries immediately rose, but Europe was a little slower to respond.

Some traders said the morning's release of Dutch August CPI figures was also mildly bullish. The CPI index fell 0.1 percent from July to 1.9 percent in August. Economists had expected the August CPI data to show a 2.0 to 2.3 percent year-on-year rise.
"The initial reaction to the figures was neutral, but, along with the U.S. figures, they provided a bit of a boost in Holland," one trader said.

However, the rises were largely driven by professional traders as the market still failed to draw in investors. Some traders said the market would need to attract end investor interest to stave off weakness early next week. However, many were not hopeful, given the low yields available.
"At the beginning of next week, we really need to have a positive start, with real buyers. Otherwise, we cannot stay at these levels," one trader said.
Friday's gains were greatest at the long end of the curve. The long Jan 2023s rose by 1.30 guilders to 108.75/108.95.
"Generally, the short stuf underperformed," one trader said.
